newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-U.S. DOMINATE HEATS BUT LOSE DOLAN.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-U.S. DOMINATE HEATS BUT LOSE DOLAN.

text.p: The United States dominated the heats at the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships on Monday but lost world record holder Tom Dolan to an asthma attack.

The United States had the top qualifiers in four of the six preliminary events in the morning, while Olympic champion Penny Heyns of South Africa topped the heats in the women's 100 metres breaststroke and Michael Klim set an Australian and Commonwealth record with the fastest time this year in the men's 100 freestyle.
But the biggest surprise of the morning was Dolan's asthma attack, which the Olympic champion suffered while swimming the men's 400 individual medley.
Dolan finished in four minutes 30.11 seconds, far off his world record of 4:12.30. American Tom Wilkens won in 4:20.47, ahead of Australians Matthew Dunn and Trent Steed.
"At the start of the breaststroke, my chest tightened and I couldn't breathe. I almost drowned in the freestyle," said Dolan, who had a two-second lead going into the last leg of the race.

It was apparent something was wrong and Dolan could be seen gasping for air as he swam the freestyle leg. Dolan also suffered an asthma attack while competing in the U.S. nationals last month and his coaches said he probably would not swim again in this meeting, which ends on Wednesday.
With Dolan fading to 13th, Ron Karnaugh, at 31 the oldest competitor in Fukuoka, took the second American place in the final.
Heyns' time of 1:08.65 was slightly better than that of her great Australian rival Samantha Riley (1:08.78), who took the bronze in Atlanta.
Kilm's record-setting time of 49.52 put him ahead of Ricardo Busquests of Puerto Rico and American Neil Walker going into Monday night's finals.
Kilm trains with Alexander Popov, the world-record holder in the event.

American Jenny Thompson topped all qualifiers in the women's 100 freestyle, but should still face a challenge from China's world- record holder Le Jingyi, although Le is not swimming with the same form when she won in Atlanta last year.

Americans also finished first and second in the men's 100 breaststroke heats and the women's 400 individual medley heats. Kristine Quance and Madeline Crippen finished on top in the individual medley, while Kurt Grote and Jarrod Marrs did a one- two in the breaststroke.
Grote's time of 1:01.31 was then ninth-fastest ever in the 100 breaststroke.
The championships have attracted about 300 swimmers from 22 countries and regions, and are one of the last important events on the swimming calendar prior to next January's world championships.
